Do not use a catheter valve when the patient cannot reliably sense bladder fullness or manage the valve (e.g., cognitive impairment, poor dexterity), has inadequate bladder capacity or high-risk urinary retention, or has a UTI, hematuria, or obstruction requiring continuous drainage. Also avoid it when continuous drainage is medically necessary, such as during acute illness, post-urologic surgery, or when accurate fluid balance monitoring is required.
